info.title: Drawer Component Skill
info.description: Side panel that slides over the page to create, edit, or inspect one entity without leaving the current view

post.description: Generate or validate a Drawer component instance with specified props

DrawerProps.description: Props for the Drawer React component. Generated from the manifest — do not edit by hand.

size.description: Drawer.Content only. Width of a left/right drawer, from the --cn-drawer-{size} tokens. Use 'sm' or 'md' for a form; 'lg' and above only when the body holds a table or side-by-side content. Never set a width through className — size is the only sanctioned width control. Not exposed as a Figma property (see DRW-001).

direction.description: Set on Drawer.Root, not on Drawer.Content: Content reads it from context and applies the matching cn-drawer-content-{direction} class. Keep the default 'right' for create/edit drawers so every drawer in the product opens from the same edge.

overlayClassName.description: Drawer.Content only. Class merged onto the overlay behind the panel. An escape hatch; a form drawer does not need it.

forceWithOverlay.description: Drawer.Content only. Renders the overlay even when the drawer is non-modal (Drawer.Root modal={false}). Has no effect on a modal drawer, which always has one.

staticStackWidth.description: Drawer.Content only. When a nested drawer opens on top, this drawer keeps its declared width instead of being pushed and resized by the stack animation.

keyboardSupport: Focus moves into the drawer when it opens and is trapped there while it is modal
Focus returns to the trigger when it closes
The header close button is reachable with Tab
x-accessibility.notes: The drawer is announced as a dialog named by its title, so every drawer needs a title — the structured header takes it as the title prop. With no description the header renders a visually hidden 'No description available' so the dialog still has a description reference; pass a real description when one helps. Do not remove the close button (hideClose) unless the footer has another way to dismiss.

correct: <Drawer.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}><Drawer.Content size='md'><Drawer.Header title='Create flag set' /><Drawer.Body><FormWrapper {...form}><Layout.Vertical gap='lg'><FormInput.Text name='name' label='Name' /></Layout.Vertical></FormWrapper></Drawer.Body><Drawer.Footer><ButtonLayout><Button variant='primary' type='submit'>Create</Button></ButtonLayout></Drawer.Footer></Drawer.Content></Drawer.Root>

x-known-gaps: DRW-001: this manifest has no figma block yet. drawer.figma.ts maps the Figma drawer's title, tagline and description, but size, direction and the stack props are not Figma properties, and the Figma node details have not been verified for this manifest

DRW-002: ds-check --source reads one file, so this manifest's props are Drawer.Content's (plus direction, which Content applies from Root's context). Root, Header, Body and Footer props are described in composition, not checked prop-by-prop

DRW-003: Drawer.Header has two APIs — the structured title prop and the older Title/Tagline/Description children. Passing title selects the structured mode; nothing in the type stops a caller also passing Title/Tagline/Description children. Pick one mode per header
DRW-004: Drawer.Footer is a plain div with no action API, so nothing enforces one primary button or a consistent order. ButtonLayout inside it is the convention, not a constraint
